description: API design rules for REST conventions, versioning, response formats, and authentication patterns

rules.message: Use kebab-case for URL paths (e.g., /user-profiles not /userProfiles or /user_profiles)
rules.design_check: Do all proposed endpoint paths use kebab-case (e.g., /vehicle-listings, /market-valuations)? Flag any camelCase or snake_case path segments.

rules.description: Avoid verbs in URL paths - use HTTP methods instead
rules.message: Avoid verbs in URLs. Use HTTP methods: GET /users not GET /getUsers
rules.design_check: Do any proposed endpoint paths contain verbs (getUsers, createOrder, deleteItem)? Replace with noun-based resources and HTTP methods (GET /users, POST /orders, DELETE /items/{id}). BLOCK on verb-in-URL.

rules.description: Limit nested resource depth to 2 levels
rules.message: Limit nested resources to 2 levels. Use query params or separate endpoints for deeper nesting
rules.design_check: Are any proposed API paths nested more than 2 levels deep (e.g., /tenants/{id}/vehicles/{id}/reports/{id}/items)? Flatten using query parameters or separate top-level endpoints.

rules.description: Never include sensitive data in responses
rules.message: Never expose passwords, secrets, tokens, or API keys in responses
rules.design_check: Does the proposed response schema include any sensitive fields (password, secret, token, apiKey, privateKey)? Remove them. BLOCK on sensitive field exposure.

rules.description: Never pass auth tokens in query parameters
rules.message: Never pass authentication tokens in URL query parameters
rules.design_check: Does the design pass authentication tokens or API keys in URL query parameters (e.g., ?token=xxx)? If so, use Authorization header instead. BLOCK.

rules.message: Avoid wildcard (*) CORS origin in production - specify allowed origins
rules.design_check: Does the design specify CORS configuration? Ensure it lists specific allowed origins rather than wildcard (*). BLOCK on wildcard CORS in production design.

rules.description: Do not return HTTP 200 for error cases
rules.message: Do not return 200 OK for error scenarios
rules.design_check: Does the design specify using HTTP 200 for error responses (e.g., success: false in body)? Replace with appropriate status codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 500). BLOCK.
